instrument: Koopman and Widen, redefining safety for autonomous vehicles
requirement_paraphrase: Argues current safety definitions assume human supervision and need revision for driverless operation (open world, self-enforced limits, ad hoc system of systems, legal/ethical constraints); contrasts ISO 26262, ISO 21448, UL 4600, DefStan 00-56.

instrument: MOIAT public consultation 'Advice: Drones' and drone product status service
status_note: Closed; no outcome listed; service page gave no requirement detail
requirement_paraphrase: Pre-market/operating requirements stated: valid Product Status Letter from the Conformity Sector, product label, serial number, no attached audio/video recording devices; categories recreational, commercial, R&D.
applies_to: Importers, sellers, operators of drones in UAE

instrument: Machinery Reg (EU) 2023/1230 as amended by Reg 2026/1744
status_note: Per EUR-Lex consolidated text of 27 July 2026 (no legal effect); Reg (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 Jul 2026, in force 27 Jul 2026. Delegation period: five years from 27 Jul 2026 (Art. 47(2)).
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 8 (new third and fourth paragraphs), Art. 20(10), Art. 47(2) (consolidated text, markers M2)
requirement_paraphrase: Commission to adopt delegated acts amending Machinery Reg Annex III with health and safety requirements for AI systems that are high-risk under AI Act Art. 6(1) and are safety components of, or themselves, machinery, reflecting AI Act Ch. III Sec. 2 and Arts 17, 19, 72, 73; the delegated acts are to apply by 2 Aug 2028. Until harmonised standards or common specifications exist under the Machinery Reg, systems complying with standards/specifications under AI Act Arts 40/41 are presumed to meet Annex III machinery requirements.
applies_to: Machinery with AI safety components, incl. robots

status_note: Applies from 20 January 2027 (Commission page; Art. 54 as corrected by corrigendum OJ L 169, 4.7.2023).
requirement_paraphrase: Commission page says the Regulation integrates provisions for machinery with AI-powered safety functions; Directive 2006/42/EC applies until then.
applies_to: Machinery incl. robots placed on EU market

instrument: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Annex I Part A
status_note: Observatory summary of final act. Its application date (14.1.2027) predates the corrigendum; the operative date is 20 January 2027.
clause_or_section_seen: Annex I Part A (category numbers 5 and 6 not verified); Art. 25(2) route seen
requirement_paraphrase: Safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning for safety functions (category 5) and machinery with such embedded systems (category 6) need mandatory third-party conformity assessment.

clause_or_section_seen: Annex III (1.2.1 per Art. 20(9); retention sub point unverified)
requirement_paraphrase: Law firm summary: safety functions must not be changed by ML beyond limits set in the risk analysis; self-learning machines must not act outside defined task and movement space; safety-decision data kept at least one year; technical file must describe limits, data, development and validation of autonomous machines. Note: the one year retention of safety decision data is not found in Arts 10, 11 or 13 and is not verified in Annex III; an unofficial reproduction places it in 1.2.1 second list point (b). The 10 year technical documentation retention in Art. 10(3) is a different rule.

instrument: NASA-STD-7009 (Standard for Models and Simulations), version B
edition_or_version: 7009B Change 1; NASA page document date given as 03/05/2024 (format ambiguous)
status_note: Active; page says 'Not a NASA Mandatory Standard'; 5-year review date shown as passed
requirement_paraphrase: Sets uniform M&S practices and credibility assessment in development and use; acceptance criteria set by program and approved by Technical Authority.
applies_to: NASA programmes using models and simulations for critical decisions

status_note: Superseded by B per NASA page
requirement_paraphrase: Requires assessing M&S results against 8 Credibility Assessment Scale factors (verification, validation, input pedigree, results uncertainty, results robustness, use history, M&S management, people qualifications) scored 0-4, and reporting caveats and uncertainty to decision makers.

instrument: NHTSA Standing General Order 2021-01 (Third Amended) crash reporting
requirement_paraphrase: Named manufacturers/operators must report ADS and L2 ADAS crashes: most severe within 5 days, others monthly; ADS thresholds stricter than ADAS; crash within 30 seconds of system use.
applies_to: Named entities in US (ADS L3-5 and L2 ADAS)

edition_or_version: Formal 2.3 (adopted Oct 2023 per OMG page); 2.4 beta listed
status_note: OMG spec page lists 2.4 as beta (informational); formal version is the one to follow for compliance
requirement_paraphrase: Defines a metamodel/UML profile for representing assurance cases (auditable claims, arguments, evidence) and a graphical notation for tool exchange.
applies_to: Tool vendors and developers exchanging assurance cases

instrument: RICS article: GNSS spoofing and mitigation in the Arabian Gulf
status_note: Professional-body practice note; not a standard
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends machine-control and robotic users configure alarms for coordinate jumps, fuse GNSS with IMU/LiDAR, use authenticated corrections, keep RTK fallback and validate time sync; surveyors to use multi-session observations and cross-checks.
applies_to: Surveyors, machine-control, construction in the Gulf

instrument: RTA Administrative Resolution No. (939) of 2025 (AV executive rules)
edition_or_version: Issued 10 Nov 2025; effective on Official Gazette publication (Art. 16)
status_note: English text is a translation; Arabic prevails
requirement_paraphrase: Covers light/heavy autonomous vehicles, buses, autonomous equipment and machinery, motorcycles. Art. 3 safety assessment: manufacturer-country compliance certificate, public-road test certificate, UAE conformity certificate, local operational test runs with data to RTA, design safety showing, RTA-approved speed/lane/zone system. Art. 4 emergency communication with Operator. Art. 14: operators notify malfunctions, store operational data securely, apply secure software updates.

status_note: In force; Annex I text not retrieved
clause_or_section_seen: Annex I Part A (item number not verified; text not returned); Art. 6(1) and Art. 25(2) seen
requirement_paraphrase: Part A list reported to include safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning to ensure safety functions, and embedded systems with such components when not separately marketed. Conformity route for Part A categories under Art. 25(2): module B plus C, module H or module G (EUR-Lex extraction, 2026-10-12). The Annex I entry itself and its number remain unverified.
applies_to: ML-based safety components and machinery embedding them

status_note: In force; Annex III 1.2.1 text not retrieved
clause_or_section_seen: Annex III 1.2.1 (existence and subject confirmed by Art. 20(9) cross reference; sub point locators for retention unverified)
requirement_paraphrase: Secondary source (MAAK) says 1.2.1 requires safety functions and settings not to be easily modifiable beyond the manufacturer's risk analysis limits, including by user changes and machine learning adjustments. Retention periods were not found in any official text read. One unofficial reproduction places a one year retention of safety related decision data in 1.2.1 (second list, point b, self evolving or autonomous machinery) and a five year tracing log of interventions and safety software versions in 1.2.1 point f. Unverified against the Official Journal.
applies_to: Machinery with control systems, incl. self-learning

status_note: In force; Annex IV headings and point list not retrieved from official source (EUR-Lex text cuts off before annexes); download Annex IV from https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1230/oj/eng
clause_or_section_seen: Annex IV Part A (content not seen); Art. 10(2) and 10(3) seen; Annex IV Part B referenced in Art. 14(7)
requirement_paraphrase: Technical file shows machine meets EHSRs: risk assessment, protective measures, residual risks, test/calculation reports; safety software source code or logic; for autonomous or sensor-fed machines, system characteristics, limits, data and validation processes.
